derivations.method: Off Duty printed 19:05/00:05Z with no '+1'. The Zulu value is printed, but its calendar date is not; 19:05 local ORD confirmed by to_utc as 2026-09-05T00:05Z, so the duty ends on the following UTC day.

Report printed 20:20/00:20Z on the 16SEP row with no '+1'. The Zulu value is printed; its date is not. to_utc confirms 20:20 local JFK on 16SEP = 2026-09-17T00:20Z, so the entire duty (report, sector and off duty) sits on 17SEP in UTC despite the 16SEP row date.
Report printed 00:25/23:25Z on the 27SEP row. The Zulu value is printed; its date is not. to_utc confirms 00:25 local LHR on 27SEP = 2026-09-26T23:25Z, so report falls on the previous UTC day.
Off Duty printed 00:27/23:27Z+1. The '+1' belongs to the local reading (00:27 on 08SEP); to_utc confirms that instant is 2026-09-07T23:27Z, so endUtc stays on 07SEP.
STA 06:35/22:35Z+1 and Off Duty 07:05/23:05Z+1 at SIN. '+1' marks the local date (19SEP); to_utc confirms 06:35 SIN on 19SEP = 2026-09-18T22:35Z, so both UTC instants remain on 18SEP.
STA 00:50/23:50Z+1 = 2026-09-20T23:50Z but Off Duty 01:20/00:20Z+1 = 2026-09-21T00:20Z (both confirmed by to_utc); the duty's arrival and its end fall on different UTC dates.

SIM row has no STA; the 16:00/15:00Z printed in the Off Duty column is taken as the end of the training window. Report is the printed start 08:00/07:00Z with no offset applied, per the standing rule for training.
